good_thing: (Aotea/Great Barrier Island, New Zealand): Eleven threatened niho taniwha, or chevron skinks, returned to the island’s Glenfern Sanctuary on November 23. Descended from three injured skinks cared for at Auckland Zoo for nearly 30 years, they were released with bamboo refuges and tiny tail transmitters to help conservation workers learn how they settle back into forest life.
current_or_history: On November 27, 1895, Alfred Nobel signed his final will at the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris. He wrote it himself and signed before four Swedish witnesses, none of them lawyers, directing most of his estate toward the prizes that became the Nobel Prizes.
tiny_fact: Tree shrews are neither rodents nor true shrews, despite the name. They are a distinct group of small mammals native to Southeast Asian forests.
thought: You do not have to make the whole day meaningful for one small part of it to matter.
